proposals.hypothesis: LiZr2(PO4)3 (NASICON-type) pairs a fully oxidized, hard-to-reduce Zr4+ cation with a phosphate framework. Unlike Li3PO4, whose contact penalty came from oxidized P/S products, and Li2O, which reacted strongly with PCl5/sulfur species, the Zr4+ and PO4 units should have less oxidative driving force against the argyrodite sulfide. It is also a wide-gap insulator, so it may keep the penalty low while being chemically distinct from the halide and Li-rich oxide families already tested.
proposals.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.337), LiF (0.310), LiBr (0.335) and Li2O (1.815) all failed, mostly from oxidative or anion-driven contact products. The best so far is the chloride family at 0.189 (bin 9), but no chloride candidates are available. A transition-metal-free, Zr4+-based phosphate offers a distinct chemistry to test whether a stable framework cation lowers the penalty.
